decided: BenchmarkRecordAccept is corrected to measure the accept path rather than de-dup hits, by forgetting the de-dup set between blocks and asserting conservation (delivered == b.N) so it can never silently drift back. That moves a published gate baseline: the accept row goes from 716 ns / 3 allocs to the real accept cost, which docs/performance.md and its 'A note on BenchmarkRecordAccept' section are rewritten to carry. Separately, Flush's biz_dropped_events_total re-credit branch gains a test on both sides — that the drop counters survive a failed metric export, and that the transaction families do not.
why: The published figure was describing the wrong path. docs/performance.md already states the defect in full and declines to fix it, on the stated ground that correcting the benchmark would move a gate baseline in the same PR that introduces the numbers proving it needs correcting. That reasoning was right for that PR and is spent now: this item exists to move the baseline deliberately, with the correction and the new number landing together. The conservation check is the part that matters beyond this fix — the benchmark drifted into measuring suppression precisely because nothing asserted which path it took, and BenchmarkRecordParallel already carries exactly this assertion for exactly this reason. On the re-credit branch: it is the single exception to Flush's failed-metric-batch policy, it protects the record of the library's own damage during a backend outage, and neither the exception nor the rule it excepts had any test.
cost_if_wrong: The gate's benchmark baseline for emit.Record moves in one step and any regression threshold pinned to the old number must be reset; a wrongly-corrected benchmark would set that threshold against the wrong path a second time, which is why conservation is asserted rather than assumed. The numbers are measured on one host and are host-specific by the document's own statement, so they are a baseline shape, not a contract. If the re-credit tests encode the wrong policy they would freeze a double-count hazard in place — mitigated by testing both sides against mutations rather than only the happy one. Nothing in production code changes: both items are test and documentation.
alternatives: Leave BenchmarkRecordAccept alone and rename it to say it measures suppression — rejected: it would then duplicate BenchmarkRecordSuppressed, and the accept path would have no single-goroutine baseline in the gate at all

Pre-build b.N unique contexts as BenchmarkRecordParallel does — rejected: that benchmark is behind //go:build benchload precisely because it is memory-heavy, and this one runs in the PR gate, where sizing an allocation to b.N invites the OOM the tag exists to avoid

Fix the benchmark but leave the published numbers for a later docs pass — rejected: ADR-0008 wants the behaviour and the docs describing it in one PR, and a stale figure is exactly the defect being corrected
Test only the re-credit's positive side — rejected: the policy is an exception to a rule, and a test that does not pin the rule cannot tell over-crediting from correct behaviour
scope: emit/emitter_test.go (BenchmarkRecordAccept's keying and its conservation check; the new re-credit test), docs/performance.md (the accept row, its label, and the note section that documents the defect), and any README figure quoting the old accept number. No change to emit/emitter.go, emit/emit.go, or any production path; the re-credit branch is tested as it stands, not modified.
